prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the pii-chat agent (card support: identity checks, lost and stolen cards, replacements) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: verifying identity on the phone. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 2)
response: {"items":[{"type":"fact","content":"When a caller gives partial details that match our records, I still complete the full identity check before discussing any card issue, so I do not rely on recognition alone."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member cannot recall one answer, I offer the next appropriate verification step rather than ending the call, because a different route can still confirm they are who they say they are."},{"type":"fact","content":"When I hear hesitation on a sensitive detail, I slow the pace and ask one question at a time, which helps the member answer more accurately and reduces avoidable errors."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the answers are confident but slightly inconsistent, I treat that as a sign to re-check the record carefully, since genuine members sometimes mix up old and current details."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a member rings from a different number, I never use the caller line as proof of identity; I always verify the person, not the phone."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member is reporting a lost or stolen card, I prefer to complete identity checks before discussing next steps, because it keeps the account secure and the conversation focused."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the security questions seem rushed, I pause the script and explain why we need them, as a clear reason usually improves cooperation and accuracy."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member has recently moved or changed contact details, the old information may still appear in our systems, so I check which details are current before treating an answer as wrong."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a call is passed between colleagues, I repeat the completed verification status clearly, so the next agent does not need to start from the beginning unless the case requires it."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the identity check is close but not fully complete, I would rather ask one extra confirming question than guess, because a cautious approach is safer than making an incorrect decision."}]}
